40425.etyen:
Borrowed from German Nazist (“Nazi”), a shortened form of Nationalsozialist (“National Socialist”); compare German Nazi (“Nazi”) and the agent-noun suffix -ist (“adherent or agent suffix”). German Nazi is itself a colloquial clipping of Nationalsozialist, formed after Sozi (“socialist; Social Democrat”). The full form Nationalsozialist is composed of national (“national”) and Sozialist (“socialist”). Doublet of nazi (“Nazi”). First attested in 1933.
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk nazist, Danish nazist, Swedish nazist, German Nazist, Dutch nazist, Romanian nazist, French naziste and Italian nazista

1000425.etyen:
From ass (“A-flat”) + -ess (“semitone-lowering suffix”), literally “A-flat-flat”. The base ass (“A-flat”) is derived from German German As (“A-flat”), itself formed from the note name A with -s, a variant of the semitone-lowering suffix -es. The Bokmål suffix -ess (“semitone-lowering suffix; flat”) is likewise derived from German -es.
Compare the parallel formations Danish ases, Swedish assess, German Ases (also Asas), Dutch ases and Finnish asas (“A double flat”).

1005033.etyen:
Compound of Lærdal (“municipality and valley in Vestland”) + elv (“river”), with linking -s- (“interfix”) and the traditional local definite singular ending -i, literally “the Lærdal river”.
The first element Lærdal is from Middle Norwegian Lærdall, from Old Norse Læradalr, probably reduced from reconstructed *Lærardalr. The latter consists of the genitive *Lærar of a lost river name *Lærr and dalr (“valley, dale”), literally “valley of the Lærr”.
